issues.description: The problem statement specifies a Book struct with a property named `title`, but the solution implementation declares the property as `bookTitle`. Meanwhile the solution's Client and assembleBookstore code use `book.title` and call the initializer as `Book(title: ...)`. This naming mismatch (title vs. bookTitle) breaks the clear mapping from the problem to the implementation, is likely to cause compilation/test failures, and will confuse students about the expected property name.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the Book property name across artifacts. Rename the solution's `bookTitle` property to `title` (e.g., `let title: String`) so it matches the problem statement and existing Client usage, or alternatively update all usages and initializers to consistently use `bookTitle`. Preferred fix: change `bookTitle` → `title` in the Book struct and keep the existing Client/initializer calls.
